title: The explicit proper-open-proper graph model of ordinary etale compact support
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of arbitrary schemes [def-pc-scheme] with a supplied factorization $X\xrightarrow{j}C\xrightarrow{c}Y$, $j$ open and $c$ proper [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Suppose also that $f=\pi e a$, where $a:X\to U$ is proper, $e:U\hookrightarrow P$ is open, and $\pi:P\to Y$ is proper. On the ordinary unbounded small-etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], there is a natural isomorphism
$$B:R c_*Dj_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi_*De_!Ra_*.$$
Here is the specified comparison, fixing more than the isomorphism class of its endpoints. Form $T=P\times_Y C$ with projections $p_1:T\to P$, $p_2:T\to C$ [def-pc-fibre-product] and $v=(ea,j):X\to T$. Put $O_1=T\times_CX$, $O_2=T\times_PU$, with open maps $b_1:O_1\to T$, $b_2:O_2\to T$. There are proper maps $s_1:X\to O_1$, $s_2:X\to O_2$ induced by $(v,1_X)$ and $(v,a)$, respectively. On $O_{12}=O_1\times_TO_2$, the induced map $s_{12}:X\to O_{12}$ is proper; its composites with the two open projections $u_1,u_2$ are $s_1,s_2$. Define
$$B_1:Rc_*Dj_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(\pi p_1)_*Db_{1!}Rs_{1*},\qquad B_2:R\pi_*De_!Ra_*\xrightarrow{\sim}R(\pi p_1)_*Db_{2!}Rs_{2*}$$
by the canonical direct-image compositors and the Cartesian proper/open interchange [lem-sf-etale-proper-open-tensor-square]. In $B_1$ insert $Rs_{1*}$ using the identity $X\to O_1\to X=1_X$; in $B_2$ insert $Rs_{2*}$ using $X\to O_2\to U=a$. Identify the two middle words by
$$Db_{1!}Rs_{1*}\cong Db_{1!}Du_{1!}Rs_{12*}\cong D(b_1u_1)_!Rs_{12*}\cong D(b_2u_2)_!Rs_{12*}\cong Db_{2!}Du_{2!}Rs_{12*}\cong Db_{2!}Rs_{2*}.$$
The first and last comparisons are the Cartesian proper/open interchange for a proper map factoring through an open immersion; the others are the canonical open compositors [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]. With this middle comparison denoted $B_{12}$, set $B=B_2^{-1}\circ R(\pi p_1)_*(B_{12})\circ B_1$, with the canonical functor associators. Direct-image compositors are those of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], normalized by the composite adjunction [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. The three maps $s_1,s_2,s_{12}$ are proper and all displayed comparisons are isomorphisms without quasi-compactness of the open maps or Noetherian hypotheses. This statement asserts no tensor compatibility of $B$.

proof.text: Use the already constructed pullback maps v, s1 and s2. The projections q1:O1→X and q2:O2→U are proper by two successive base changes of π and c, respectively, hence separated. The pullback projection equations give s1≫q1=1_X and s2≫q2=a. Rewrite these composites to give them properness instances, then apply Mathlib IsProper.of_comp to get IsProper s1 and IsProper s2. This proves the first two fields without invoking any derived-category existence theorem.

source.place: Tags 01W4 and 01W6(2); the graph construction in LowerShriekComposition.lean lines 199–220

proof.text: The intersection graph s12 is the existing pullback lift of s1 and s2. Its first projection u1 is an open immersion by base change of b2, itself the base change of e. Thus u1 is separated. The equation s12≫u1=s1 makes the composite proper by the first step. Apply IsProper.of_comp once more to conclude that s12 is proper. This replaces the longer identity-top Cartesian-square argument; it applies to arbitrary schemes and open immersions.

With the two properness instances from step 1, the explicitly defined locallyClosedGraphIso is available. Its definition is exactly Side1 followed by the associator, the whiskered Middle, the inverse associator and the inverse of Side2, using the published upstream open-exchange, open-composition and adjunction-normalized direct-image comparison APIs. Supply this very isomorphism as the comparison field, step 2 as properS12, and reflexivity as comparison_eq. The other properness fields are supplied by step 1. Wrap the record in Nonempty. No generic tensor-compatibility or coherence assertion is needed to assemble this record, and no witness is chosen from an unproved existence theorem.
